feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Hungary's only nuclear power plant shut down completely for the first time in its history
entry.summary: The Paks plant, which normally supplies close to half of Hungary's electricity, went fully offline on 2 August as the Danube fell to a record low in Budapest. — Sources: Al Jazeera, 2 August 2026 · euronews, 30 July 2026 · Associated Press wire reporting, August 2026 · enerdata, 26 August 2026

entry.title: France cut a larger share of its nuclear fleet to drought than previously reported
entry.summary: France's electricity utility cut output from 12 percent of its entire nuclear fleet on 4 August, naming three further reactors beyond the shutdowns already reported, as river levels used for reactor cooling fell further during the summer's drought. — Sources: energynews.pro, August 2026 · Industrial Info Resources, August 2026

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany dipped again, continuing an uneven recovery
entry.summary: Germany's main shipping gauge read 16 centimetres on 15 October, down from 18 centimetres the day before. — Sources: Kaub gauge readings, direct fetch via rivercruise.ai, 15 October 2026

entry.title: Singapore's air quality returned to moderate, though forecasters warn it could worsen again this weekend
entry.summary: Singapore's 24-hour air quality index fell into the moderate range by the morning of 14 October, improving from the season's worst reading of 191 recorded on 9 October. — Sources: National Environment Agency Singapore, 13-14 October 2026

entry.title: Malaysia offered Indonesia firefighting aircraft and helicopters to fight the region's haze-causing fires, still unanswered
entry.summary: Malaysia's government offered one firefighting aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help Indonesia contain the fires behind the region's transboundary haze. — Sources: Malay Mail, 10-11 October 2026

entry.title: Malaysia's haze eased enough that two states reopened schools
entry.summary: Twenty-one Malaysian air-quality monitoring stations recorded unhealthy readings on 13 October, down from nine stations that breached a stricter threshold on 9 October. — Sources: Bernama, 13 October 2026 · The Vibes, 13 October 2026
